scenarios.sql: WITH counts AS (SELECT m.customer_id,m.customer_name,COUNT(r.account_id) record_count FROM customers m LEFT JOIN accounts r ON m.customer_id=r.customer_id GROUP BY m.customer_id,m.customer_name) SELECT customer_id,customer_name,record_count FROM counts WHERE record_count>(SELECT AVG(record_count) FROM counts) ORDER BY record_count DESC,customer_id;

scenarios.question: Find customers whose every orders is Active.
scenarios.pseudo: I will require that each customers has at least one record. I will use NOT EXISTS to exclude masters with a non-Active record.
scenarios.sql: SELECT m.customer_id,m.customer_name FROM customers m WHERE EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM orders r WHERE r.customer_id=m.customer_id) AND NOT EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM orders r WHERE r.customer_id=m.customer_id AND r.status<>'Active') ORDER BY m.customer_id;

scenarios.question: Find orders above the average order_total for their status.
scenarios.pseudo: I will compare each record with the average amount for its own status.
scenarios.sql: SELECT order_id,status,order_total FROM orders r WHERE order_total>(SELECT AVG(x.order_total) FROM orders x WHERE x.status=r.status) ORDER BY status,order_total DESC;

scenarios.question: Calculate days between the first and last event for each orders.
scenarios.pseudo: I will group events per record and take minimum and maximum dates. I will subtract the first date from the last date to get active days.
scenarios.sql: SELECT r.order_id,MIN(e.item_date) first_event,MAX(e.item_date) last_event,MAX(e.item_date)-MIN(e.item_date) active_days FROM orders r JOIN order_items e ON r.order_id=e.order_id GROUP BY r.order_id ORDER BY r.order_id;

scenarios.question: Calculate every event's percentage contribution to its orders total.
scenarios.pseudo: I will divide each event amount by the total amount within its record partition.
scenarios.sql: SELECT order_item_id,order_id,amount,ROUND(100.0*amount/NULLIF(SUM(amount) OVER(PARTITION BY order_id),0),2) record_percent FROM order_items ORDER BY order_id,order_item_id;

scenarios.question: Return the highest-value customers in each segment.
scenarios.pseudo: I will total record amounts for every master and segment. I will row-number masters within each segment and keep rank one.
scenarios.sql: WITH totals AS (SELECT m.customer_id,m.customer_name,m.segment,SUM(r.order_total) total_amount FROM customers m JOIN orders r ON m.customer_id=r.customer_id GROUP BY m.customer_id,m.customer_name,m.segment), ranked AS (SELECT *,ROW_NUMBER() OVER(PARTITION BY segment ORDER BY total_amount DESC,customer_id) rn FROM totals) SELECT customer_id,customer_name,segment,total_amount FROM ranked WHERE rn=1 ORDER BY segment;

scenarios.question: Find customers whose record count is above the average master record count.
scenarios.pseudo: I will left join and count records for every master in a CTE. I will keep counts above the average master count.
scenarios.sql: WITH counts AS (SELECT m.customer_id,m.customer_name,COUNT(r.order_id) record_count FROM customers m LEFT JOIN orders r ON m.customer_id=r.customer_id GROUP BY m.customer_id,m.customer_name) SELECT customer_id,customer_name,record_count FROM counts WHERE record_count>(SELECT AVG(record_count) FROM counts) ORDER BY record_count DESC,customer_id;

scenarios.question: Show completed, pending and failed event totals per orders.
scenarios.pseudo: I will conditionally sum Completed, Pending and Failed event amounts per record.
scenarios.sql: SELECT r.order_id,SUM(CASE WHEN e.status='Completed' THEN e.amount ELSE 0 END) completed_amount,SUM(CASE WHEN e.status='Pending' THEN e.amount ELSE 0 END) pending_amount,SUM(CASE WHEN e.status='Failed' THEN e.amount ELSE 0 END) failed_amount FROM orders r LEFT JOIN order_items e ON r.order_id=e.order_id GROUP BY r.order_id ORDER BY r.order_id;
